text:
**Countries that had 75 – 90 % Internet use for the *entire* period 2010 – 2020**

| Country | 2010 (World Bank – IT.NET.USER.ZS) | 2015 (World Bank – IT.NET.USER.ZS) | 2020 (World Bank – IT.NET.USER.ZS) |
|---------|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Austria | 75.17 % | 83.94 % | 87.53 % |
| France  | 77.28 % | 78.01 % | 84.71 % |
| Germany | 82.00 % | 87.59 % | 89.81 % |

These three economies were the only ones that kept their individual‑level Internet penetration consistently between 75 % and 90 % (inclusive) across **2010, 2015 and 2020**.

---

### How the data were obtained  

The World Bank API was queried for the indicator **IT.NET.USER.ZS** (“Individuals using the Internet (% of population)”) for the three years of interest:

| Year | API request used* |
|------|-------------------|
| 2010 | `https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/IT.NET.USER.ZS?format=json&per_page=2000&date=2010` |
| 2015 | `https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/IT.NET.USER.ZS?format=json&per_page=2000&date=2015` |
| 2020 | `https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/IT.NET.USER.ZS?format=json&per_page=2000&date=2020` |

The responses were filtered to keep only the records whose countries had a **non‑null** value that lay in the 75 – 90 % range for all three years.  The table above lists the resulting values for each qualifying country.

\*The raw JSON payloads returned by the API contain each country’s value for the requested year; the values displayed in the table were extracted directly from those payloads.
